description: Earliest known concept/build in the Alfr3d lineage.
Early 2014 iteration of the home-automation daemon.
2014 iteration, ordering relative to MK-I/MK-II unconfirmed.
Home-automation daemon running on a Pi (/home/alfr3d/alfr3ddaemon.py), audio handling.
Added Python LIFX integration (pylifx).
Server + mobile companion apps split out: Alfr3dServer, Alfr3d4Android-Original, Alfr3d-MKIII-Android, alfr3d.io.
Separate repo from the 2015 MK-IV Notion page, not yet reconciled with it.
First Kafka message-bus architecture (topics speak/environment/device/user); direct architectural precursor to today's Kafka-based backend. Undated.
Repo explicitly describes itself as "Successor to Project Alfr3d" — a rebrand attempt that didn't end up replacing it. Undated.
Now Littl3-1-Engineering/alfr3d, 279 commits, latest tagged release v0.1.7. Described by its own README as "the final resting place of Alfr3d after years of different architectures and repos."
Product site for Littl3.1 Engineering with Alfr3d as flagship. Pages: index.html, alfr3d.html, lab.html.

Containerized microservices (Kafka, MySQL, Redis, FastAPI, React), Nexus/Domain/Matrix frontends, Spotify integration, RTSP streaming, WHEN/IF/THEN automations, situational-awareness engine, IoT sync. Functionality shipped in code though not yet git-tagged.
28 tagged releases, free spatial launcher + $5.99 Pro unlock live, CI builds debug APK on every push to main, signed-release workflow on version tags.
Core free / Nexus Launcher free+$5.99 Pro / Cloud Phase 3 $5.99-$11.99 / Kit unscheduled, published on littl31.com/alfr3d.html.
All 3 repos (alfr3d, alfr3d_deck, Littl31) migrated from personal armageddion account to the Littl3-1-Engineering org.
Remote-access relay (no port forwarding) + push notifications; "thin, dumb-pipe relay" that never sees plaintext data. Not yet built.
RELEASE_NOTES.md already documents v0.1.8 ("Situational Awareness Registry") but the latest actual git tag is still v0.1.7.

Signing, Gradle Play Publisher, and gated CI already wired up; blocked on manual account-holder steps: Play developer enrollment, Play Console app entry, first manual release upload, sensitive-permission declarations + demo video, hosted privacy policy URL, CI service account for future automated releases.
Pre-flashed Raspberry Pi appliance, built to order. Parked until Alfr3d Cloud proves demand. Not yet scheduled.

Corrected: repo does have a LICENSE file (FSL-1.1-ALv2 text, matches the site). GitHub's NOASSERTION was a license-detector classification gap for a non-SPDX-standard license, not a missing file. No action needed.
Push notifications to the launcher; depends on Alfr3d Cloud Phase 3 shipping first.
No accessible public roadmap/issue list found for the site itself — unconfirmed.
